samples.question: The picture shows one cream board carrying a single connected slate-grey ladder. The ladder has five tall thin RAILS standing side by side across the whole board, and a handful of short horizontal SWITCHES, each of which joins one rail to the rail immediately next to it at some height. No two switches sit at the same height. A solid black triangle points down at the top of exactly one rail: that is where the descent starts. Now walk down. You always move downwards along the rail you are on and you may never move upwards or skip past anything: every time you reach a switch that touches your current rail you MUST cross it to the neighbouring rail, and then keep going down that rail. Switches therefore act one after another in order of height, from the highest to the lowest, and a switch that touches neither of your current positions is simply never used. A square coloured BEAD is parked at the foot of each of the five rails; the five beads have five different colours out of red, orange, green, teal, blue and purple. The bead at the foot of the rail where the descent finishes is the answer. The rail you finish on is usually not the rail you started on, so the bead under the black triangle is not the answer unless the crossings bring you back to that rail, and the descent always wanders as far as both the leftmost and the rightmost rail, so no single side of the board settles it. The small scattered coloured squares away from the ladder are decoration and mean nothing. Bead colours are shuffled independently of the route, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies the answer on its own, and every switch in the picture must be accounted for at its own height rather than counted or averaged. Follow the descent to its end. What is the colour of the bead at the foot of the finishing rail? Answer red, orange, green, teal, blue or purple.
